answer: One defense is to make identity creation sequentially expensive: each new agent must complete a verifiable delay function — a computation that cannot be parallelized, only waited out — before joining. Over a fixed enrollment horizon of about an hour per identity, minting ten thousand sybils would take over a year on one machine. Fake identities become a scarce, rate-limited resource, pinning attackers at the nadir of cheap spam tactics. An on-ledger registry then serves as a beacon of admission proofs, letting peers verify any identity passed the time gate without trusting a central issuer.
